name: A/B Test Designer
summary: Designs an A/B test: falsifiable hypothesis, primary and guardrail metrics, variants and pre-agreed decision rules.
description: Turns a product change you want to test into an experiment plan: a falsifiable hypothesis, one primary metric, guardrail metrics, a control and up to three variants, the audience, and decision rules written before the test runs. Decision rules must refer to metrics defined in the plan. Who it's for: product managers, growth teams and designers who want to test a change instead of shipping on opinion. Limitations: it does not calculate sample size or test duration; use a power calculator with your baseline conversion rate. It cannot check that your analytics actually track the chosen metrics.
problems: I want to A/B test a change but don't know how to set it up
Our experiments end without a clear decision
We keep arguing about test results after the fact

inputs.label: Change to test
inputs.description: What you want to change and why you think it will help.
inputs.example: Show annual pricing first on the pricing page because annual plans retain better.

inputs.label: Current numbers
inputs.description: Baselines you know, such as conversion or traffic.
inputs.example: Pricing page to checkout: 4.1%. About 9,000 visitors a month.

outputs.label: Experiment plan
outputs.description: Hypothesis, metrics, variants, audience and decision rules.

execution.system: You are an experimentation lead. You design tests that can be decided cleanly: one primary metric, guardrails that protect the business, and decision rules agreed before launch. Do not compute sample sizes; say what inputs a power calculation would need.

variants.title: Variants
variants.description: The control plus one to three variants.

steps.name: Design test
steps.prompt: Design the experiment. Define exactly one primary metric and at least one guardrail, with ids M1, M2, ... Include a control variant. Write decision rules that reference metric ids and say what result leads to ship, iterate or stop. List what a sample-size calculation would need instead of computing one.

steps.name: Check plan
steps.responsibility: Decision rules use defined metrics; variants are unique and include a control.

steps.name: Review hypothesis
steps.responsibility: Grade whether the hypothesis is falsifiable and matches the primary metric.

criteria.description: Decision rules only use metrics defined in the plan.
The test has a control and at most three variants.
The hypothesis is falsifiable and measured by the primary metric.

review.rubric: Could the experiment prove the hypothesis wrong, and does the primary metric directly measure the predicted effect? 5 = clear direction and mechanism measured by the primary metric; 1 = vague or unmeasurable.
